prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / game character pose.
Produce ONE separate transparent PNG for Char, cast #01. Image 1 is her USER-APPROVED likeness-v2 MASTER and the primary identity, art style, costume, adult body proportions, build and hair reference. Preserve this exact character; this is a new pose, not a redesign. Do not use photographs or a realistic portrait face.

LOCKED ART: expressive anime/cartoon brown eyes, tiny simplified nose, friendly stylized smile where the face is visible, softly shaded illustrated skin, long wavy brown hair, cream headband and long hair ribbon; cream lace high-collar blouse and cuffs, cameo, puffed sleeves, burgundy sash/side bow, elaborately folded teal-green floor-length skirt, modest jewelry and brown shoes. Rich deliberate pixel clusters, crisp dark warm outlines, same upper-left neutral key light, detail and flattering cartoon face as approved. Do not shrink the eyes, add portrait realism or detailed teeth, change costume colors, elongate her anatomy or compress her into a tiny chibi body.

GEOMETRY: same elevated three-quarter mansion game camera and grounded adult anatomy. Orient the WHOLE BODY in the requested direction: head/nose, chest, hips, knees and shoes agree. This is a stationary IDLE, not walking or a stride. Author this direction; do not simply mirror the approved picture. Preserve physical costume asymmetry: for this directional review, interpret the approved burgundy side bow and larger ribbon knot as on Char's anatomical RIGHT, which is image-left in a front-facing view. Carry that same physical side into back/profile views; far-side details may be hidden rather than moved.

COMMON SCALE: use a portrait canvas matching the reference proportions, ideally its 916 x 1716 pixels. Preserve one common drawing scale/head size across all seven poses. Standing figure should fit comfortably inside with crown and shoes clear of edges, about 88â€“90% of canvas height. Do not crop hair, ribbon, sleeves, hem or shoes. No background shadow.

OUTPUT: one complete character only, genuine transparent RGBA, with transparent padding around every extremity. No chair or stool, furniture, floor, scenery, cast shadow, text, labels, border, comparison panel, additional character, held object or modern accessory. All limbs remain complete for later furniture occlusion. This is a review draft, not final runtime art.

SEATED OVERRIDE TO STANDING FRAMING: The following seated geometry and shorter occupied-height instructions take precedence over the standing-framing sentence above. Do NOT enlarge a seated body to standing height.

POSE seated_idle_east: Char is genuinely SEATED, facing EAST / SCREEN RIGHT. Her pelvis rests on an invisible chair seat, torso upright, hips and knees bent naturally about 90 degrees, thighs projecting right, lower legs down and both shoes grounded. Long skirt drapes over the bent knees and falls naturally to the feet; it must visibly describe a seated lap, not a standing cone or kneeling pose. Her hands rest gently together on her lap, no object. Face/nose/gaze and chest point right. Image 2 is ONLY FURNITURE GEOMETRY REFERENCE: the LOWER red chair on the far left, approximate background rectangle [4,166,44,57] in the 480x320 kitchen image. It is chair_east; exact target g_kitchen::kitchen_lower_chair_01::seat. The seat is a contact, not the floor. Do not paint ANY chair or background into the output. Preserve the same head and torso drawing size as the standing reference: seated occupied height should be roughly 65â€“72% of standing height. On the same portrait canvas leave substantially more transparent space ABOVE her rather than zooming/enlarging the seated body to fill the canvas. Aim crown around y=430, pelvis/seat around y=1080, shoe floor around y=1600 on a 916x1716 canvas. These are layout guides, not labels.
